prompt: Let $f(x) = \frac{x^2 - 1}{x - 1}$. At which $x$-value is $f$ NOT continuous?
hint: A function cannot be continuous at a point where it is not even defined. Where is the bottom zero?

hints.text: A function cannot be continuous at a point where it is not even defined. Where is the bottom zero?
$x = 1$. The function is undefined there, so it is not continuous at $x = 1$ (it has a hole).

explanation: Continuity at $a$ requires, first of all, that $f(a)$ exists.
The denominator $x - 1$ is zero at $x = 1$, so $f(1)$ does not exist.
Everywhere else $f(x) = x + 1$, a smooth line. The only break is at $x = 1$.

alternativeExplanations.title: See the hole
steps: So the graph is the line $y = x + 1$ with one point punched out, at $(1, 2)$.
The limit at $1$ is $2$, but the value is missing — a removable discontinuity.
